newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian peso closes lower at 1,002.20.
newsitem.headline: Colombian peso closes lower at 1,002.20.

text.p: Colombia's peso snapped a seven-day winning streak and closed 2.0 lower at 1,002.20 after warnings from Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo that the central bank would intervene in the country's interbank market as much as necessary to halt the buoyant currency's recent rise.

Traders said the peso had continued to strengthen early in the session on dollar-sales by coffee and oil exporters. But its its early gains were cut by a cumulative demand for about $10 million from the corporate sector.
There was also sporadic demand for greenbacks from the banking sector, dealers said.

Ocampo, who spoke to reporters after a weekly policy meeting with the central bank's board of directors, said board members had agreed to intervene more aggressively in the interbank market in a bid to undercut the peso.

The currency has risen sharply since early June, when it was trading at 1,074 to the dollar, prompting repeated requests from the government and exporters for a devaluation to help make Colombian goods more competitive in the global marketplace.
Ocampo said the central bank had purchased $49 million on the interbank market this week to halt the peso's rise.
There was no sign of central bank intervention in Friday's trading, however, dealers said.
They reported an active 367 trades for a total of $151 million and said the peso held in a 995.50 to 1,002.40 range.
